sections.content: Here are the first words for what we eat and drink. You already know *víz* (water) and *kávé* (coffee); now add the foods. To say that something is there, use *van*, and for “there is none” use *nincs*. The word stays in its basic form, and Hungarian does not need “some”: *Van kenyér.* means “There is bread.”

sections.title: One thing or just “some”
sections.content: *Egy* (a, an) is for one single piece: *Van egy alma.* (There is an apple.) For more than one, add *-k* as you know it: *Vannak almák.* (There are apples.) Bread, milk, cheese and soup have no *egy* here, because we do not count them one by one.

items.english: There is coffee, tea and water.

sections.content: English says “some bread” or “any milk”. Hungarian says only *kenyér*, *tej*. In this form (nothing added to the end) the word just names the thing; the next screen shows what changes when someone does something to it.
